libchromeos-ui: chromium_command_builder: add flag for passive event listeners This CL adds a bit of logic to chromium command builder to add the "--passive-listeners-default=true" flag if the correct USE flag was set for this board. The USE flag is "passive_event_listeners". That that USE flag is found in /etc/ui_use_flags.txt (set based on the USE flags for that board during build time) when starting Chrome, then --passive-listeners-default=true will be added to the Chrome command line. CQ-DEPEND=CL:387745,CL:387726 BUG=chrome-os-partner:57500 TEST=I emerged and deployed libchromeos-ui onto my Kevin. By looking at chrome://version I could see the command line and check that the right flag had been added. When I retried after removing the USE flag, the command line when back to normal. I followed up using rbyers.net/eventTest.html and "inspect"ed the main area's touchstart event listener. This correctly identified the listeners as passive or not passive as the case may be for my tests. Change-Id: Icbf989d2e856935dc536ebf4e29fdd00d87b2578 Signed-off-by: Charlie Mooney <charliemooney@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/387747 Reviewed-by: Dan Erat <derat@chromium.org>

chromeos_config: Remove local config instances. Instead of creating local BuildConfig instances, always use templates. This proved a bit awkward because we compare builder names against the 'base' template name. So... beaglebone-release should use the template 'release'. Still, this CL means we only use template to create build configs, which will make it easier to break apart the _GetConfig method. Tweaked config_lib to allow template names to be explicitly overridden. A later CL will adjust SiteConfig.Add so that the base config is always explicitly stated, which should be cleaner. Ran "bin/cbuildbot_view_config --full | grep -v _template" and saw no changes with/without the CL.
